clients.notes: Genesis agents client. Signs requests via vault-bound Ed25519 keypair (cato/vault_crypto.py, CATO_AP2_PUBKEY). Rotated a second time on 2026-08-13 after a root-cause investigation (Vault.create() in cato/vault.py unconditionally deleted the existing vault.enc on any recreate, with no guard against overwriting real data) found the vault had been repeatedly recreated that morning. The 00:00:00Z key C0b5/ct/FoXrZ99mBj+LsDAPQGw3kBLFvl+ZlnvwDIg= belonged to one of those short-lived intermediate vaults (2-4 credentials, missing GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN and others) and was never confirmed to have completed a real accepted call before the vault was recreated again. A genuine last-known-good vault.enc backup from 2026-08-12T16:53:28Z (10 real credentials, sha256 fd06e909195a345529dfda0d01edf14d3b04060e7077bea7617a39df181d75e5) was recovered intact using the operator's current CATO_VAULT_PASSWORD and restored as the live vault, bringing back this earlier keypair (7G6FdR1...) rather than generating a fresh one, since a real trusted identity with a verified private key beats an untested new one. C0b5/ct/... is DELETED, not disabled, for the same reason the 2026-05-17 key was deleted below: its private half lived only in a vault generation that no longer exists and no operator controls it. Vault.create()/unlock() now refuse to silently overwrite or auto-create an existing vault (see cato/vault.py and tests/test_vault_safety.py) — this class of incident should not recur.
